source.title: HTML Accessibility API Mappings 1.0, W3C Working Draft, 21 October 2026

elements.title: area (no href attribute)
elements.comments: User agents MAY still expose an a element lacking the href attribute with a link role in the event an author specifies interactive behavior for the element. For example, if using an event handler attribute.

elements.title: aside (scoped to the body or main element)
elements.html: aside (scoped to the body or main element)

elements.title: aside (scoped to a sectioning content element)
elements.html: aside (scoped to a sectioning content element)
elements.aria: complementary role if the aside element has an accessible name. Otherwise, generic role.

elements.title: autonomous custom element
elements.aria: If the author assigned a conforming ARIA role using the role attribute, map to that role. Otherwise, the generic role.

elements.title: b
elements.comments: Exposed by platform specific bold font weight text styles.

elements.title: bdi
elements.comments: IA2/ATK: May affect on "writing-mode" text attribute on its text container.

elements.title: bdo
elements.comments: IA2/ATK: Exposed as "writing-mode" text attribute on its text container.

elements.title: body
elements.comments: User agents MUST ignore the aria-hidden attribute if specified on the body element.

elements.title: br
elements.comments: May be exposed as '\n' character by the platform interface.

elements.title: button
elements.comments: A button's mapping will change if the aria-pressed or aria-haspopup attributes are specified.

elements.title: caption
elements.comments: NoteIf a caption element is hidden from the accessibility tree, then it will not provide an accessible name to its parent table element.

elements.title: datalist (represents pre-defined options for input element)
elements.html: datalist (represents pre-defined options for input element)
elements.aria: listbox role, with the aria-multiselectable property set to "true" if the datalist's selection model allows multiple option elements to be selected at a time, and "false" otherwise
elements.comments: If datalist is not linked to a proper input element, then datalist element is not mapped to accessibility APIs.

elements.title: dd
elements.computedRole: Use WAI-ARIA mapping NoteEditorial Note: This value may change upon resolution of ARIA #1662.

elements.title: dialog
elements.comments: See also the dialog element's open attribute.

elements.title: dir (obsolete)
elements.comments: The dir element is marked as obsolete in HTML, and is not to be used by authors.

elements.title: dl
elements.computedRole: list NoteEditorial Note: This value may change upon resolution of ARIA #1662.

elements.title: dt
elements.computedRole: Use WAI-ARIA mapping NoteEditorial Note: This value may change upon resolution of ARIA #1662.

elements.title: fieldset
elements.comments: NoteIf a legend element is hidden from the accessibility tree, then it will not provide an accessible name to its parent fieldset element.

elements.title: footer (scoped to the main element, or a sectioning content element)
elements.html: footer (scoped to the main element, or a sectioning content element)
elements.comments: User agents and assistive technology MAY not expose the sectionfooter role if the element: has no accessible name is not keyboard focusable has no other global ARIA attributes or HTML attributes that expose information to user agent's accessibility tree

elements.title: form
elements.comments: If a form has no accessible name, do not expose the element as a landmark.

elements.title: form-associated custom element
elements.aria: If the author assigned a conforming ARIA role using the role attribute, map to that role. Otherwise, the generic role.

elements.title: h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, and h6
elements.html: h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, and h6
elements.aria: heading role, with the aria-level property set to the number in the element's tag name.

elements.title: header (scoped to the main element, or a sectioning content element)
elements.html: header (scoped to the main element, or a sectioning content element)
elements.comments: User agents and assistive technology MAY not expose the sectionheader role if the element: has no accessible name is not keyboard focusable has no other global ARIA attributes or HTML attributes that expose information to user agent's accessibility tree

elements.title: hgroup
elements.comments: If an hgroup contains multiple heading elements, then the user agent MAY treat the heading element with the highest priority level as the sole heading of the hgroup. The user agent MAY expose all other heading elements as if they were p elements. See paragraph role on Core AAM.

elements.title: hr
elements.comments: If an hr element is a descendant of a select element, user agents MAY expose the element with a role of none.

elements.title: html
elements.comments: User agents MUST ignore the aria-hidden attribute if specified on the html element. NoteThe document role of a web page is not exposed by the html element, but rather from a parent document node created by the user agent.

elements.title: i
elements.comments: Exposed by platform specific italic text styles.

elements.title: img
elements.comments: NoteARIA 1.3 adds the image role as the preferred synonym to the ARIA 1.0 img role. The expected computed role for named img elements is now "image".

elements.title: img (alt attribute value, when trimmed of whitespace, is the empty string, i.e., alt="", alt=" ", or alt with no value in the markup)
elements.html: img (alt attribute value, when trimmed of whitespace, is the empty string, i.e., alt="", alt=" ", or alt with no value in the markup)
elements.comments: Note If an img has an empty alt, but has been provided an accessible name via another valid naming mechanism per the naming steps of this specification, user agents will expose the element with its implicit image role.

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Button state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Button state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Checkbox state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Checkbox state)
elements.aria: checkbox role, with the aria-checked state set to "mixed" if the element's indeterminate IDL attribute is true, or "true" if the element's checkedness is true, or "false" otherwise

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Color state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Color state)
elements.comments: If implemented as a color picker, any UI controls presented for selecting a color are exposed in the accessibility tree, associated with the input element, and mapped as appropriate for the type of control (e.g., button or slider).

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Date state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Date state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Local Date and Time state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Local Date and Time state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the E-mail state with no suggestions source element)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the E-mail state with no suggestions source element)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the File Upload state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the File Upload state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Hidden state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Hidden state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Image Button state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Image Button state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Month state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Month state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Number state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Number state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Password state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Password state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Radio Button state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Radio Button state)
elements.aria: radio role, with the aria-checked state set to "true" if the element's checkedness is true, or "false" otherwise. With aria-setsize value reflecting number of type=radio input elements within the radio button group and aria-posinset value reflecting the elements position within the radio button group.

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Range state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Range state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Reset Button state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Reset Button state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Search state with no suggestions source element)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Search state with no suggestions source element)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Submit Button state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Submit Button state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Telephone state with no suggestions source element)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Telephone state with no suggestions source element)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Text state with no suggestions source element)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Text state with no suggestions source element)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Text, Search, Telephone, URL, or E-mail states with a suggestions source element)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Text, Search, Telephone, URL, or E-mail states with a suggestions source element)
elements.aria: combobox role, with the aria-controls property set to the same value as the list attribute

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Time state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Time state)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the URL state with no suggestions source element)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the URL state with no suggestions source element)

elements.title: input (type attribute in the Week state)
elements.html: input (type attribute in the Week state)

elements.title: label
elements.comments: Note If a label element is hidden from the accessibility tree, then it will not provide an accessible name to the labelable element it is associated with.

elements.title: li
elements.aria: listitem role with aria-setsize value reflecting number of li elements within the parent ol, menu or ul and aria-posinset value reflecting the li elements position within the set.
elements.comments: If li element is not an accessibility child of an ol , menu or ul, or if the containing list element is no longer exposed with a list role, then expose the li element with a generic role.

elements.title: math
elements.comments: Mapping for math is defined by MathML AAM 1.0.

elements.title: menu
elements.comments: The menu element is a semantic alternative to the ul element. It has no implemented mappings or behavior that reflect the semantics of the ARIA menu role. Note obsolete menuitem element and menu with type attribute.

elements.title: option (in a list of options or represents a suggestion in a datalist)
elements.html: option (in a list of options or represents a suggestion in a datalist)
elements.aria: option role, with the aria-selected state set to "true" if the element's selectedness is true, or "false" otherwise.

elements.title: output
elements.comments: AXDescription: value from associated label element subtree.

elements.title: param
elements.comments: param is obsolete in HTML

elements.title: progress
elements.aria: progressbar role, with, if the progress bar is determinate, the aria-valuemax property set to the maximum value of the progress bar, the aria-valuemin property set to zero, and the aria-valuenow property set to the current value of the progress bar

elements.title: q
elements.comments: ::before and ::after CSS pseudo content is used by platforms to render the element's quotation marks.

elements.title: section
elements.aria: region role if the section element has an accessible name. Otherwise, the generic role.

elements.title: small
elements.comments: Exposed by platform specific font size styles.

elements.title: style
elements.comments: Note: There are instances where CSS properties can affect what is exposed by accessibility APIs. For instance, display: none or visibility: hidden will remove an element from the accessibility tree and hide its presence from assistive technologies.

elements.title: summary
elements.computedRole: If the element is the first child of its type within a parent details element: html-summary Otherwise, if it is not the first child of its type of a parent details element, or it is not a child of a details element: generic role
elements.comments: If a summary element is not a child of a details element, or it is not the first summary element of a parent details, then user agents MUST expose the summary element with a generic role (see HTML summary element).

elements.title: svg
elements.comments: Mapping for svg is defined by SVG Accessibility API Mappings. See also Graphics Accessibility API Role Mappings

elements.title: td (ancestor table element has table role)
elements.html: td (ancestor table element has table role)

elements.title: td (ancestor table element has grid or treegrid role)
elements.html: td (ancestor table element has grid or treegrid role)

elements.title: textarea
elements.aria: textbox role, with the aria-multiline property set to "true"

elements.title: th (is not a column header, row header, column group header or row group header, and ancestor table element has table role)
elements.html: th (is not a column header, row header, column group header or row group header, and ancestor table element has table role)

elements.title: th (is not a column header, row header, column group header or row group header, and ancestor table element has grid or treegrid role)
elements.html: th (is not a column header, row header, column group header or row group header, and ancestor table element has grid or treegrid role)

elements.title: th (is a column header or column group header)
elements.html: th (is a column header or column group header)

elements.title: th (is a row header or row group header)
elements.html: th (is a row header or row group header)

elements.title: title
elements.comments: A title element provides the accessible name for its document.

elements.title: u
elements.comments: Exposed by platform specific underline text styles.
